title: CLO 2024.2 - Hair Cluster Generator
description: CLO2024.2 New Hair Clump Generator — Generate default hair maps to create realistic clustered hair! Easily control complex hair details and use the Hair Clump Generator to produce more realistic and natural hair clumps!
transcript:
To facilitate users in creating hair loss effects, we launched the Hair Loss Vinegar Generator in version 2024.2.  
By using this feature, users can define and generate multiple hair loss effects by themselves.  
Additionally, to improve usability, we have also provided 15 hair loss presets in Connect Business City, allowing users to use them directly.  
In this video, I will introduce the Hair Loss Vinegar Generator in detail and demonstrate how to apply the desired hair loss effect.  

First, open the project file.  
Drag the hair loss prediction adjusted from Connect or pre-adjusted by yourself to the object window and apply it on the board.  
Select the hair loss material.  
In the property editor, before opening the Hair Loss Generator, basic parameters such as hair material and hair type have already been set.  
Then scroll down.  
Find the default image.  
Click the hair loss option next to the default image.  
Open the Hair Loss Generator window.  

In the Hair Loss Generator, there are two default images: the long-distance image and the curved-direction image.  
You can adjust both images to easily generate hair loss effects.  
Click on the long-distance image and the curved-direction image with the mouse to view them.  
On the left is the corresponding default preview effect,  
and on the right are the adjustable attributes.  
These parameters can be adjusted in any way,  
and you can preview the generated default effect on the left.  

First, let’s look at the length chart.  
Under the attributes on the right side of the length chart,  
there are two attributes: the cutting chart and the editing effect.  
If these two attributes are not visible in the menu,  
you can click the small triangle on the left to expand.  

The cutting chart and editing effect are used to set the length effect of hair vinegar.  
First, let’s examine the cutting chart.  
The cutting chart is mainly used to show different hair lengths within the same texture pattern.  
It contains four parameters: mode, image level, low area length, and high area length.  
Currently, these four parameters are grayed out.  
To make them adjustable,  
the cutting chart must be added here.  

Next, let’s explain each parameter separately  
for better understanding and application.  

First is the mode.  
It includes RGB and alpha modes.  
Select RGB10.  
The hair length depends on the grayscale level of the cutting chart.  
The cutting chart must use grayscale.  
In this context, the black area indicates the shortest hair length,  
and the white area indicates the longest hair length.  
If you choose alpha mode,  
the hair length depends on the transparency level of the cutting chart.  
The cutting chart must have transparency applied.  
The transparent area indicates the shortest hair length,  
and the opaque area indicates the longest hair length.  

Next, let’s look at the image level.  
This adjusts the intensity of the grayscale.  
Increasing the value makes the cutting effect more pronounced.  

Next are the low area length and high area length.  
These two parameters adjust the shortest and longest hair lengths, respectively.  

Next, let’s examine the editing effect.  
The editing effect includes intensity and randomness.  
First, intensity.  
The higher the intensity value,  
the greater the difference in hair length from the edge to the center,  
creating sharper hair effects.  

Below intensity is randomness.  
This adjusts whether the hair length over the entire fabric surface is consistent or irregular.  
The higher the value, the more inconsistent the hair length becomes,  
and the distribution of long and short hairs becomes irregular.  

Next, let’s look at curve distribution.  
Open the curve direction chart.  
It includes two properties: hair loss and hair loss details.  

First, click on hair loss.  
Hair loss creates the effect of individual hairs being missing.  
It contains four parameters: intensity, hair loss density, random direction intensity, and randomness.  

Next, let’s explain each parameter separately  
for better understanding and application.  

First is intensity.  
This property adjusts the intensity of hair loss along each curve direction.  
The higher the intensity, the more obvious the hair loss and the stronger the three-dimensional effect.  

Next is hair loss density.  
This adjusts the density of hair loss.  
A higher value means higher hair loss density,  
with smaller, closer hair loss spots.  
A lower value means lower density,  
with larger, more scattered hair loss spots.  

Regarding random direction and random intensity,  
these two parameters control whether the curve direction of hair loss is consistent or irregular.  

Next, click on hair loss details.  
Hair loss details adjust the detailed effect of each hair loss spot.  
It contains five parameters.  
The first four parameters function similarly to those previously described,  
so no further explanation is needed.  

Finally, the intensity of hair loss increase adjusts the concentration of each hair loss spot,  
while keeping the direction of each hair loss unchanged.  
Higher intensity results in more focused hair loss.  
With the highest density setting, hair loss appears smooth and loose,  
as if tidied up.  

Next, we will adjust this hair loss effect following the meanings of the attribute parameters explained earlier.  

First, let’s see how to adjust the hair loss effect based on the preview.  
Open the length chart.  
Because this hair loss effect does not require displaying hair loss of different lengths,  
there is no need to use the cutting chart.  

This hair is a bit sharp on each side, so increase the strength slightly; 0.3 is fine.  
You can drag the slider or enter the value directly.  
The length of each hair is called the rule.  
So keeping the value within the range of 0.1 is good; 0.08 works well.  

After adjusting the length chart, proceed to the bend direction chart.  
Let’s look at the hair vinegar first.  
The hair vinegar shows a certain three-dimensional effect, so adjust the strength value to about 0.45.  
The hair vinegar density is not very high, so set the density to 0.2.  
The bending direction and bending strength of the hair vinegar are both called rules, so keep these at 0 or enter 0.05.  

Next, let’s look at the hair vinegar details.  
The previous four parameters can be set according to the direction of the hair vinegar.  
First, adjust the detail effect of the single hair vinegar accordingly.  
Adjust the values based on the desired effect.  

Finally, looseness.  
Since the hairs in the single hair vinegar are slightly open, set looseness to 0.45 here.  

After adjusting the properties of each parameter, be sure to click Apply first and then Close.  
The property settings made earlier will be applied to the hair.  

Finally, open the synchronization rendering in the rendering window to view the final effect.  
If there are no issues, output the rendered image.  

Next, I will show you the final rendered hair image.  

Now, let’s see how to set the hair effect presenting a partial flower shape.  
Open the Hair Vinegar Generator.  
Go to the cutting image under the length image.  
Add the pre-made black-and-white flower-shaped image.  
Note that the cutting image must be a grayscale image.  
For example, the mode should be set to RGB mode.  

After adding, the following properties can be adjusted according to the desired effect.  
For example, if you want the hair vinegar in the flower-shaped area to be clearer and more distinct,  
adjust the image level to an appropriate value, such as 0.65.  
If you want a certain length of hair in the low area,  
adjust the low area length accordingly, for example to 0.2.  

After adjusting the properties, click Apply and then Close.  
Open the rendering window and run synchronization rendering.  
Check the final effect.  
If there are no issues, output the rendered image.  

Next, I will show you the final rendered hair image designed with a partial flower shape.  

We believe that the application of the new hair preset and Hair Vinegar Generator by Kinect will enhance your design experience and expand your creativity.  
We look forward to your use of the Hair Vinegar Generator to experiment with hair designs.  

Thank you for watching.  
See you next time.  
Thank you for watching.

chunks.content: ## Overview of Hair Loss Vinegar Generator in CLO 2024.2 This section introduces the Hair Loss Vinegar Generator, a feature launched in CLO version 2024.2 that enables users to create customizable hair loss effects. It includes 15 preset hair loss styles available in Connect Business City for direct use, enhancing both creativity and usability. --- ## Getting Started with Hair Loss Vinegar Generator To begin using the Hair Loss Vinegar Generator: - Open your project file in CLO. - Import a hair loss prediction map from Connect or use a pre-adjusted map. - Apply this map to the hair object in the object window. - Select the hair loss material. - In the property editor, ensure basic hair parameters like hair material and hair type are set. - Scroll to find the default image section and click the hair loss option to open the Hair Loss Generator window. --- ## Hair Loss Generator Interface and Default Images The Hair Loss Generator provides two default images for creating hair loss effects: - **Long-distance image:** Controls hair loss effects viewed from afar. - **Curved-direction image:** Controls hair loss effects following hair curve directions. Users can click either image to preview the default effect on the left panel while adjusting attributes on the right. Changes update the preview in real time. --- ## Length Chart: Cutting Chart and Editing Effect The Length Chart includes two expandable attribute groups essential for hair length effects: ### Cutting Chart - **Purpose:** Displays varying hair lengths within the same texture. - **Parameters:** - **Mode:** Choose between RGB and Alpha modes. - *RGB mode:* Uses grayscale where black = shortest hair, white = longest hair. - *Alpha mode:* Uses transparency where transparent = shortest hair, opaque = longest hair. - **Image Level:** Controls the intensity of the grayscale effect; higher values increase cutting effect strength. - **Low Area Length:** Sets the shortest hair length. - **High Area Length:** Sets the longest hair length. Note: Parameters are initially grayed out and become adjustable only after adding the cutting chart. ### Editing Effect - **Intensity:** Controls the gradient of hair length difference from edge to center; higher values create sharper hair length contrasts. - **Randomness:** Adjusts uniformity of hair length distribution; higher values increase irregularity in hair length across the fabric. --- ## Curve Distribution: Hair Loss and Hair Loss Details The Curve Distribution section contains two key properties for detailed hair loss effects: ### Hair Loss - **Purpose:** Simulates missing individual hairs along hair curves. - **Parameters:** - **Intensity:** Controls strength of hair loss effect and 3D appearance. - **Hair Loss Density:** Adjusts how dense or sparse hair loss spots are; higher density means smaller, closer spots. - **Random Direction Intensity & Randomness:** Determine whether hair loss directions are uniform or irregular. ### Hair Loss Details - **Purpose:** Refines detail for each hair loss spot.

chunks.title: CLO 2024.2 - Hair Cluster Generator
chunks.content: --- ## Curve Distribution: Hair Loss and Hair Loss Details The Curve Distribution section contains two key properties for detailed hair loss effects: ### Hair Loss - **Purpose:** Simulates missing individual hairs along hair curves. - **Parameters:** - **Intensity:** Controls strength of hair loss effect and 3D appearance. - **Hair Loss Density:** Adjusts how dense or sparse hair loss spots are; higher density means smaller, closer spots. - **Random Direction Intensity & Randomness:** Determine whether hair loss directions are uniform or irregular. ### Hair Loss Details - **Purpose:** Refines detail for each hair loss spot. - **Parameters:** Five parameters similar to Hair Loss, plus: - **Hair Loss Increase Intensity:** Controls concentration of each hair loss spot without changing direction, producing smoother, tidier hair loss at high values. --- ## Procedure for Adjusting Hair Loss Effects 1. **Length Chart Adjustment:** - If uniform hair length is desired, omit the cutting chart. - For sharper hair edges, increase intensity (e.g., 0.3). - Set overall hair length rule within 0.1 (e.g., 0.08). 2. **Curve Direction Chart Adjustment:** - Set hair loss intensity around 0.45 for strong 3D effect. - Adjust hair loss density to ~0.2 for moderate spot concentration. - Maintain bending direction and strength near 0 or 0.05. 3. **Hair Loss Details:** - Adjust parameters to refine individual hair loss spots. - Set looseness to around 0.45 for slightly open hair strands. 4. **Apply Settings:** - Click **Apply** then **Close** to save adjustments. - Use synchronization rendering in the rendering window to preview the final effect. - Export the rendered image if satisfied. --- ## Creating Custom Hair Loss Shapes (Flower Shape Example) To design partial hair loss effects shaped like a flower: 1. Open the Hair Loss Vinegar Generator. 2. Under the length image section, add a grayscale flower-shaped cutting image. 3. Set mode to RGB for proper grayscale interpretation. 4. Adjust properties such as: - **Image Level:** Controls clarity of the shape (e.g., 0.65). - **Low Area Length:** Controls minimum hair length in the shape (e.g., 0.2). 5. Click **Apply** and then **Close**. 6. Run synchronization rendering to preview the effect. 7. Export the rendered image if the result is as desired. --- ## Summary and Recommendations The Hair Loss Vinegar Generator in CLO 2024.2 provides powerful, customizable tools for creating realistic hair loss effects using adjustable grayscale and transparency maps. The interface allows fine-tuning of hair length variation, hair loss density, and directional randomness, supporting both uniform and complex partial hair loss designs. Using the included presets or custom images like grayscale shapes expands creative possibilities, enhancing hair styling workflows with detailed control over hair loss appearance. For best results, always apply changes and preview with synchronization rendering before final output. ---
